summary: M5-S01 (type ui) built: three Queue-scoped Case list views, the Escalated Open Cases report and its Support Operations report folder, plus package.xml at 67.0 and an undeclared deploy-order.md. Both declared checkers exit 0 at the scopes the plan declares, all 6 XML files parse, and check-outputs is ok. One substantive gap is recorded rather than guessed: the report ships WITHOUT its Escalated criterion, because no cited skill documents the report column code for Case.IsEscalated, so as written the report returns open Cases from the last 30 days rather than escalated open Cases. A second finding: the plan's declared folder filename (reports/Support_Operations-meta.xml) is not a filename check_report_inventory.py recognises, so the folder half of the step's own report test never executes.

Not HIGH because the report is incomplete against Q91; not LOW because check-outputs is ok, nothing landed outside artefacts/M5-S01/, and the gap is named rather than filled.

deliverables.content: Six sections: what the step produces; SS 2 the seven UNVERIFIED items with U1 (absent Escalated criterion) raised first and its one-retrieve remedy; SS 3 the declared-folder-filename finding with both measured checker runs; SS 4 order (groups, then queues, then the object and its field, then the standard Cases report type; folder before report inside the step); SS 5 eight decisions including the Tier 1 pull-view/A7 position, the auto-created rival view, the sharedTo-not-public choice and the subscription warning; SS 6 two validate-only commands (source-dir and manifest) as text for a human.

process_observations.observation: Every queue this step's views point at was already built with a matching public group, so each view could be given an explicit sharedTo audience instead of defaulting to a public view nobody signed off.

M4-S04's escalation-monitoring-note.md specified the report's filters, grouping, columns, owner and cadence in a table, so the report's design came from an upstream artefact rather than from this agent's reading of the requirement.

The report ships without the Escalated criterion its own name and Q91 promise, because the report column code for Case.IsEscalated is in no cited file; as written it over-reports, and the over-reporting is silent.

The folder filename the plan declares is not one check_report_inventory.py recognises, so the folder's accessType and folderShares are never checked: measured this run, the declared name scans 1 file and the skill-documented .reportFolder-meta.xml name scans 2, both exit 0.

Deploying these three views leaves two list views per queue in the org, because every queue auto-creates one; the build has no record of which of the pair is authoritative beyond this step's deploy-order note.

Tier 1 gets a pull list view although Q31 answers that Tier 1 has work pushed to it, which is correct only while M3-S05 stays blocked on Q32-Q35; nothing in the plan says what happens to this view when Omni-Channel ships.

The step's acceptance_tests[0] description states that at step scope the checker exits 1 because main() returns 1 on any finding including INFO; measured this run it prints exactly the predicted INFO line and exits 0, since main() returns 1 only on ERROR or under --strict.
The four declared acceptance tests plus the always-on xml and manifest checks are the tester's to execute and record, not this agent's.
